headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill directs the State Corporation Commission to ensure that large energy users, like data centers, bear the costs of grid expansion and capacity, preventing these expenses from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Governor's Action Deadline 11:59 p.m., May 23, 2026 on 2026-04-22
supporters: Residential consumer advocacy groups, environmental groups, Governor Spanberger, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Sen. Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy (as amended).
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users, Data Center Coalition (initially, due to language concerns).
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill, HB 1393 (and similar SB 253), aims to shift the costs of grid expansion and capacity onto large energy users, such as data centers, to reduce residential electricity bills. If passed, analysts project residential customers could save over $65 annually, while data centers' costs would increase by roughly 16%.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill requires water users supplying data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption data, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (e.g., Potomac Conservancy, Friends of the Rappahannock), local communities, water conservation advocates, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to compliance burden), some business groups.
news_headline: Four data center bills await governor's signature as Southwest Virginia projects spark debate
news_summary: SB 553, among other data center bills, increases reporting requirements for water usage by data centers, aiming to bring transparency to their water consumption. This legislation is supported by those concerned about the environmental impact of data centers on local water resources.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes new permit processes for high-energy use facilities, requiring site assessments that evaluate noise impacts on nearby residences and schools, and allows localities to consider other environmental and land-use effects.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residential groups near proposed data centers, environmental groups (e.g., Piedmont Environmental Council), Del. Josh Thomas.
opponents: Data center industry, land developers (due to increased regulatory burden and potential siting restrictions).
news_headline: As data center noise concerns grow, Loudoun Co. officials discuss possible mitigation efforts
news_summary: Concerns over data center noise are growing in Northern Virginia, with residents reporting constant hums affecting their quality of life. HB 153 addresses these issues by requiring noise impact assessments for new high-energy use facilities and allowing localities to set stricter zoning and noise ordinances.
